title: Vilasa 7. Lokanatha and Bhugarbha
html:
The descent of Mahaprabhu's companions: Vishvarupa and Nityananda; Lokanatha comes to Mahaprabhu in Navadvipa; a confidential talk on Radha's mood and the reason for sannyasa; teachings on raga and the mission to Vrindavana; the journey of Lokanatha and Bhugarbha

1Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya, glory to Nityananda!
Glory to Advaita-chandra, glory to the host of Gaura's devotees!

2Glory, glory to Sri Jahnava, glory to Virachandra!
Those lotus feet are my shelter.

3Glory to the hearers! Listen with one mind,
give ear to a most wondrous account.

4Whatever I have written here is all true;
I write at the command of the Prabhu, my shelter.

5I write all this about the cause of the descent;
hearing it, you will find joy, and your pain will leave you.

6When Krishna descended in Vraja,
the scriptures proclaimed it as Vraja and Vrindavana.

7It is written that the circle of Vraja is eighty-four kroshas;
everywhere in it dwell Krishna's companions.

8That same Krishna descended as the Lord of Navadvipa,
with mother, father, servants, friends and girl companions.

9First of all Vishnu himself descended:1
in Shantipur appeared Advaita, the crest-jewel [of devotees].

10He is the crest-jewel of devotees, and so he is called Acharya;
through him [all the Prabhu's work] was accomplished.2

11Madhavendra and others — twenty-four sannyasis:
eight, eight and eight more3 — these are treasures of prema.

12All of them are Krishna's family in Vraja;
all who came with him I shall describe in detail.

13Four kinds of friends and servants, five kinds of girl companions —
all this I write by command from the Prabhu's holy mouth.

14Who was who before and after, and what each one's true identity was —
to avoid controversy I have written no more of it.

15As I was commanded by the Prabhu to write,
so with deep faith I write it fully.

16Shachi Thakurani, wife of Jagannatha Mishra —
know that her first son was Vishvarupa.

17His beauty had no equal, and he was very learned;
seeing and hearing him, his mother and father rejoiced.

18The house of Shachi's father was at Belpukhuria;
it is needed for the story, and so I write of it.

19Yogeshvara Pandita was her father's eldest son,
[then came] Ratnagarbha Pandita; Shachi was younger than they.

20His son, Lokanatha Pandita, rich in virtues,
went along with Vishvarupa wherever he went.4

21They studied in one place with great delight;
what became of him I shall write a little at the end.

22Both mother and father held [Vishvarupa] as dear as life;
after some days he came into Advaita's company.

23He expounded the scriptures and spoke of much learning,
and in a short time plainly became a great scholar.

24Weary of worldly life, he went off to distant lands;
his father and mother weep, their life nearly at an end.

25He gave up shikha and sacred thread and took the staff,
and wore a kaupina and ruddy cloth.

26His name became Shankararanya Puri;
what shall I say of all his kinds of virtue?

27Pandita Lokanatha became his disciple;
he visits the holy places with him and serves him constantly.

28After two years he attained perfection;
this, it is said, was the doing of Yogamaya herself.5

29In Rarh there is a village called Ekachakra;
there lived a brahmana rich in virtues —

30Hadai Pandita; his wife was Padmavati;
from her womb came the birth [of the Lord].

31On the day of Rama-navami she conceived,
and the joy in the hearts of mother and father grew boundless.

32Day by day the child grew in the womb, and ten months passed;
the joy of the brahmana and his wife kept growing.

33In the month of Magha, in the bright fortnight, on the thirteenth day,
with every auspicious sign he was born at that moment.

34They named him Nityananda, and all rejoiced;
at times he would stay stock-still, at times laugh aloud.

35For fourteen years he played from house to house;
one day a sannyasi came to the house.

36[Hadai] fed him with a joyful heart;
pleased, the sannyasi spoke these words:

37"Hadai Pandita, hear my request:
give me one alms — I have need of it."

38"As you command," he agreed.
"Give me as alms this son of yours.

39In my old age he will take me round the holy places;
you will have every happiness — do not grieve."

40Stricken by the parting, he placed his son in his hands,
and the sannyasi at once took Nityananda away with him.

41He made him his disciple, but he did not take the staff,
and wandered with him in the guise of an avadhuta.

42His heart was overflowing with the mood of Nanda's son;
what he did, where he stayed — he had no outward awareness.

43That great soul was Ishvara Puri himself.6
One day he smiled and said to Nityananda:

44"We have wandered through all the holy places there are;
do this one thing, my son, and all will be accomplished:

45the son of Nanda has descended in Navadvipa;
seek him out with a joyful heart."

46I write the simple account — [elsewhere] it is told at length;
just to hear it brings happiness and boundless joy.

47Sankarshana and Balarama are one and the same being;
Vishvarupa and Shankararanya are a difference of form in different kalpas.7

48At home his name was Nityananda, in the ashrama Avadhuta;
in the same way the son of Nanda is the son of Shachi.

49All of Mahaprabhu's own companions descended [before him];
I write of them as I heard from the Prabhu's mouth.

50After them he descended in Shachi's womb,
and the devotees descended in various lands.

51On the full-moon day of Phalguna, at an auspicious moment, was the birth;
thus Mahaprabhu grew day by day.

52As on the earth all the rivers and streams
come and meet together in the ocean,

53so to Gaurachandra, the ocean of prema,
[the devotees] come one by one and join him with joy in their hearts.

54East of Navadvipa is a land called Yashohara;8
listen further, I shall tell of it.

55In it is a village called Talagadi;
there was born one named Lokanatha.

56His father was named Padmanabha Chakravarti,
his mother was named Sita, the abode of every virtue.

57They were high kulinas, as everyone in the land knew;
with great care they had their son educated.

58In that land there was no scholar to equal him;
day by day more virtues entered into him.

59His mother and father were anxious, seeing his state:
"If our son stays at home — that is our great hope."

60They prayed especially to God
that Lokanatha should suffer no hardship.

61A great fear constantly gripped his mother and father:
"If only by some good fortune our son would stay at home!"

62They wished to get him married with all care;
seeing his parents' efforts, he reflected in his mind.

63He thinks: "How am I to leave worldly life?" —
and every impulse of renunciation arose in his heart.

64Constantly he remembers Chaitanya's feet;
his mind longs: "I shall go and see him."

65In the month of Agrahayana, in the cold, having lain down to sleep,
he took counsel within his own heart.

66At midnight he left the house and went out,
and went eight kroshas; morning came.

67Rising, his mother and father did not see him
and wept long with stricken hearts.

68That pain, that sorrow cannot be told;
he alone knows it in whose heart it arose.

69Meanwhile he reached Navadvipa
and walked slowly, pondering.

70Asking people the way, he goes to the Prabhu,
thinking in his mind: "What shall I do, what shall I say?

71When I see the Prabhu I shall tell him who I am;
but who knows whether the Prabhu will be kind to me?"

72Saying this, at times he weeps and walks slowly on:
"Accept me!" he says, "Lord of my life!"

73The Prabhu is seated, with devotees all around —
Gadadhara, Srivasa, Murari and many more.

74Beholding the Prabhu's form, he weeps
and bows, his heart overflowing with prema.

75He joins his palms, but what is he to say? No words leave his mouth;
at that moment the Prabhu rushes to embrace him.

76"O Lokanatha, you have forgotten me!
How have you spent your time, to what lands did you go?"

77Saying this, Gaura weeps as he embraces him:
"It seems fate has brought me a treasure.

78I had been as one blind, forgetting everything."
Lokanatha weeps, clasping the Prabhu's feet.

79Taking Lokanatha by the hand, he seated him beside him;
now he gazes at his face, now he laughs.

80There too he met the Pandita;9
bowing, the two embraced.

81"Having seen with my own eyes such a jewel as you,
after so many days my eyes have been blessed with good fortune."

82All were in great joy, rapt in talk about Krishna;
no one had outward awareness, all floated in the ocean of prema.

83He met Nityananda, Advaita and all the others;
he bowed to them and they embraced him.

84Thus for five nights his meeting with the Prabhu went on;
they relished much talk about Krishna and kirtana.

85One day the Prabhu said: "Listen, Lokanatha:
how did you leave worldly life and come here?"

86He told in every detail how he had come:
"All sorrow is unreal; these feet alone are real.

87How I could break free I do not know:
you put the rope of mercy around my neck and drew me here."

88Thus Mahaprabhu, sitting in seclusion,
called Lokanatha and gave him a command.

89Holding his hand, he said: "Listen, Lokanatha:
to whom shall I tell the sorrow that rises in my heart?

90Why have I come, and where are you all?
That work is not being accomplished, and my heart aches.

91To Nityananda, Advaita and all the devotees
I shall speak to each according to his realization.

92But the realization of my own heart — to whom shall I tell it?
Seeing me, some revile me, some go away laughing.

93Taking on Radhika's mood I have come to Gauda,
[…] a joy boundless and special.10

94For my sake Radha gave up caste, family and wealth;
leaving everything, she surrendered her very self.

95She made me the lord of her life; in separation from me
day and night she pines for my beauty and my virtues.

96Her body has become like a lotus-stalk fibre,
her clothing soiled, she wanders like a madwoman.

97Hundreds and hundreds of times she blames the Creator:
'He did not give me a hundred thousand eyes, as I wished.'

98With her eyes she looks on no other man's face;
she hears of my virtues and speaks of them with her mouth.

99She is ever restless for union with me,
and speaks of it so much from grove to grove on the Yamuna's bank.

100I am a rogue, impudent, an utter libertine,
turning truth into untruth, a cheat and a deceiver.

101And yet, if she sees me face to face,
her pique departs and she feels a hundred thousand joys.

102And if on some day there is no meeting with me,
a moment's separation she reckons as a hundred yugas.

103She whose love is such, whose longing is such —
even the scriptures cannot tell such virtues of hers.

104She who sports in Vrindavana is my beloved;
she is my life, and I am her life.

105For her sake I dwell in Vrindavana,
and day and night I think of her play.

106That rasa of which friends, servants, father and mother are deprived,
that rasa which enchants [me] — only the sakhis know it.

107For her virtues and her love I remain in her debt;
this I have told you, Lokanatha.

108That is one sorrow of my heart; hear another thing:
seeing me, a certain brahmana went away reviling me in every way.

109Earlier he committed an offence against me;
it has borne fruit, and he does not know it.

110Not knowing that Krishna is the guru of the world,
he wanders about drunk with false pride.

111He says that Krishna's body is [nothing…],11
and, leaving such feet of Krishna, clings to another shelter.

112From his12 mouth [the brahmanas] were born, yet he does not accept it;
he worships one thing, says another, and drinks wine.

113Holding Krishna's power, he is mighty in the world,
yet what Vyasadeva wrote he twists into something else.

114He will not call Krishna guru, but worships a maidservant;13
for this offence how many will go to Yama's abode!

115Having left Krishna, his mind has lost its strength;
he does not know that such a person is lower than a shudra.

116That is one sorrow, and there are other matters too;
I shall tell — hear a little of the reason for this.

117Between lies the month of Pausha; in the bright fortnight of Magha,
on the third day, I shall take sannyasa, for all to see.

118All brahmanas accept the staff-bearer as their guru;
I have told you this firm resolve of my heart.

119Truly, for the sake of these brahmanas I shall take sannyasa,
leave home and wander from land to land.

120That is the outward reasoning; and now the intent of my heart —
listen, Lokanatha, I tell it to you for certain.

121The whole purpose is to take on Radhika's mood;
who will understand, who will hear what is in my heart?

122The colour of my body Radha wears as her clothing —
that is why blue garments give her such delight.

123In separation from me she wears ruddy cloth
and ever regards herself as my own maidservant.

124For my sake Radha and her companions,
distraught in separation, were ready to give up their lives.

125I too shall give up my life for her sake;
that state will come — you will remain and hear of it.

126I shall take on her lustre and wear ruddy cloth,
and with a joyful heart become her servant.

127That is why I shall clothe my body in ruddy cloth;
I shall chant her virtues — so I have told you.

128All her virtues I can never repay,
even if I had a lifespan of a hundred births on earth.

129For her virtues and her love I have become her debtor;
this I have told you, Lokanatha.

130I shall flood the world with her fame and glory —
then I shall know that she has shown me such mercy.

131I shall attain her prema, my eyes will weep,
and, grey with dust, I shall dance in sankirtana."

132Saying this, Gaura-raya weeps aloud
and, crying "Radha! Vrindavana!", rolls on the ground.

133Lokanatha held the Prabhu in his arms and calmed him;
but as he spoke of Radha's virtues, he began to tremble.

134"How much sorrow, how much joy — my heart knows;
only the groves of Vrindavana are witness to it.

135Rise at dawn and go to Vrindavana;
after you will come Rupa and Sanatana,

136and those named Sri Gopala Bhatta and Raghunatha Bhatta,
and then Raghunatha Dasa, a treasury of virtues.

137All gathering together in Vrindavana,
they will describe the lila in books and perform their own bhajana.

138As I have told you, so I shall tell Rupa,
and send him off, infusing him with power.

139I shall say more — hear what is in my mind:
as that shelter is, so is the attainment, and so the bhajana.

140To make it firmer still I say it again:
when one hears from the guru's mouth, everything becomes certain.

141The lila that is my cherished goal — that is the worship;
can other people come to know it?

142You are the crest-jewel of the wise, you know every secret;
still I shall tell you the essence of that dharma.

143The scriptures speak of full, fuller and fullest;
the difference of forms points to a difference in substance.14

144There are two kinds, svakiya and parakiya;
hear also the views on this.

145All the women of Dvaraka are called svakiya;
among the parakiya, know that the gopis are the best.

146The maidens devoted to the vow of Katyayani —
know for certain that they are in that same Vraja.

147Among them there are two chief group-leaders in Vraja:
Radha and Chandravali are there.

148The natures of the two are of two kinds:
Radha and hers are vama, Chandravali dakshina."15

149As he spoke, another state came over the Prabhu;
holding Lokanatha's hand, he began to speak:

150"There is one desire of my heart, a kind of corollary;
in that which is of gain to me you shall be my helper.

151In another body the perfected devotee forgets the lila
and regards himself as entirely like prakriti.16

152Chaitanya himself instructs him,
and as he listens he remembers everything.

153Such is the Prabhu's mercy to the perfected devotee;
only he whose mind is firm knows it.

154What I shall do, what I shall say, the word of my heart —
that will become the renowned scripture in every way.

155When I send Rupa and Sanatana to Vrindavana,
they will reflect on many books and treatises.

156All of you together will approve it well;
let no one slight it — that would grieve me."

157Lokanatha said: "Prabhu, I beg of you:
dispel my doubt and purify my mind.

158Vyasadeva wrote many books
and set forth in them the bhajana of Krishna.

159But not all of that accords with this way of bhajana;
give your command, Prabhu, I bow before you."

160"Kalas, amshas, vilasas and the rest are one self, one form;
hear what is the nature of each one's lila.

161Descriptions of all this in the scriptures are endless,
but the worship of Vraja is not set out in detail there.

162Dasya, sakhya, vatsalya, madhura — the essence of the moods;
here no one accepts aishvarya.17

163And to compose on the mood of madhurya —
no one's mind enters into that.

164The way of madhura no one knows;
madhura is known to him to whom its account is [revealed].

165One qualified for another rasa does not know this love —
in it is the lila of the hero with his beloved.

166Radha's dear attendants know its bounds;
no one else knows its greatness.

167This parakiya lila is most profound;
no one else knows its inner heart.

168The Bhagavata, the Puranas and the rest are Vyasa's descriptions;
in them power and majesty are made manifest.

169All this bhajana he did not set forth;
what is set forth there is aishvarya and the like, mixed with knowledge.

170So that people might be careful in entering [the path],
he wrote in them of the excellence of Krishna's bhajana.

171Where each one dwells, with whom each stays —
who has the power to describe it?

172Sri Rupa saw Krishna's lila with his own eyes;
still I shall infuse [him] with power.

173For firmness, what he hears from his guru's mouth
he will describe with joy and delight.

174From the scriptures and converse with the saints deep prema arises;18
one surely leads to the company of the other.

175He will bring many scriptures, and their intent will be shown;
when the events of the lila are set forth, the meaning will be understood.

176He will place established proofs among them;
seeing firm statements, all will accept them.

177Where that rasa is not found in those scriptures,
he will write the word of his heart, full of rasa.

178Just now he19 is in the king's presence;
in my mercy I shall send him after you.

179All will be together in that Vrindavana
and spend their time together relishing the lila.

180They will propagate the worship of Vraja in the scriptures,
by which the son of Nanda is attained.

181What should and should not be done, what is gain and what is loss —
hearing this, all people will take shelter.

182In this is my joy; this is the word of my heart;
and then whatever I say will fully agree with that.

183Age after age people worship Krishna,
but who attains Radhika's feet?

184All those firm scriptures of many kinds —
hearing them, I shall have boundless joy.

185I myself shall be intoxicated and intoxicate20 the people of the world —
for this my heart pines every moment —

186so that people may attain Radhika's two feet
and practise bhajana and remembrance, leaving sorrow and grief behind.

187For your sake I shall beg alms of her;
to whom else shall I tell the sorrow of my heart?

188Wherever the lord of Radha's life performs his lila,
there, together with all the sakhis —

189I have no power to describe it.
I am a poor sannyasi, and I have a need:

190I shall eat myself and distribute to all the people of the world;
let them know that you have made me rich with your wealth.

191In my sorrow you will be sorrowful, in my joy joyful;
whenever anything happens, write and send me news.

192And I shall write and send to all of you,
and through those letters you will know what is well and what is ill.

193Go to that place, your own Vrindavana;
if I have the good fortune, I shall get to see [it]."

194I am ignorant and foolish — how much of this can I write?
I write what I have heard; devotees, do not find fault.

195"Hear something more, O steadfast one;
what I say, hear with a steady mind.

196If one gives up everything — the dharma of varna and ashrama —
he alone knows the inner essence of that dharma.

197One who holds to varna and ashrama does not have exclusive shelter,
and Krishna himself does not accept him.

198After staying some days in Nilachala I shall come to Gauda,
and, having renounced everything, wander in the garb of a pauper."

199Lokanatha said: "Prabhu, I beg of you:
hearing from your holy mouth, doubt is dispelled.

200Hearing this, my heart was amazed;
I have a request — please accept it.

201If such followers of varna and ashrama go beyond varna,
then all will take shelter at Krishna's feet.

202Whoever worships whomever, he accepts him;
having taken shelter, where will the soul go?"

203The Prabhu said: "Lokanatha, listen once more:
what you have asked — hear it to the end.

204[People of] the four varnas and ashramas took shelter in Krishna;
[hear] by what bhajana Krishna shows them mercy.

205Hear it carefully, with a steady mind:
the scriptures to be read and the intent of the saints are deep.

206He who can understand gains Krishna's company;
whoever transgresses [this order] is broken by it.

207The people of Vraja do not regard Krishna as God:
they always serve him in love and float in prema.

208For that joy they gave up everything;
and they have one more mighty saying:

209the mark of raga is that it does not take the reasoning of scripture;
he who does thus attains that treasure.

210He who, abandoning karma, performs bhajana turned towards raga,
attains such feet.

211He who in body, speech and mind holds another view
does not attain Vraja — that is another aim.21

212If one does this, all those moods are attained in this body;
if not, the nature of sadhana is attained in another body.

213Lokanatha, you have forgotten your own nature:
who you are, where you dwell, what your mood is,

214in which group you are, what your name is,
whom you serve, wholly absorbed.

215You are the sakhi Manjulali, of old a companion of Radha;
your service is to anoint her body and put on her girdle of bells.

216You are ever at play with Radhika,
and, regarding yourself as a maidservant, you serve her constantly.

217Happy in Radhika's happiness, sorrowful in her sorrow —
such is the renowned sakhi devoted to service."

218As he heard this from the Prabhu's mouth, everything was revealed to him;
gazing at his face, he began to weep.

219"Intoxicated with that rasa, stay in that place;
save my life — go to Vrindavana.

220Girikunda, Govardhana, Javata, Varshana,22
Sanketa, the secluded groves, all the places of the lila:

221live in those places and your heart will be happy;
leave your attachment to me and set out on the road.

222Dwell there where your birthplace is,23
perform bhajana and remember Kishora and Kishori.

223Chir-ghat, Rasa-sthali, the rows of kadambas,
and to the east of them a grove of supreme sweetness.

224Tamala, bakula and banyan trees grow there;
live in that place and your heart will be happy.

225Rasa-sthali, Vamshivata, Nidhuvana —
rest in the midst of Dhira-samira.

226Bathe in the Yamuna, live on alms you do not ask for,
perform bhajana and remembrance, and teach living beings.

227Become perfected — from you a branch will spring,
and its followers will be past counting.

228Rupa and the others of your circle will soon come together;
then you will know [everything], when all are gathered."

229The night passed; in the morning the Prabhu was seated;
saying something to Lokanatha, he seated him beside him.

230The Prabhu said: "Lokanatha, go to Vrindavana;
all sorrow will leave you and you will find your own happiness.

231I have told you the pain of my heart only as instruction."24
Rising, the Prabhu embraced him with love.

232He prostrated himself, and [the Prabhu] placed his feet on his head,
and then began to weep, holding his hand.

233"I have given you my own land, Vrindavana, as a gift."
Lokanatha lost outward awareness and began to weep.

234Who but the master and the servant can understand all this?
Who knows what the two of them experienced?

235Gadadhara Pandita was there;
his disciple Bhugarbha made a request:

236"Prabhu, command me too to go to Vrindavana;
I have had this wish for many days — be merciful."

237Mahaprabhu said: "Gadai, give your leave:
let Lokanatha and Bhugarbha go together."

238Gadadhara said: "Bhugarbha, go with him;
the two of you will go happily, delighting in talk about Krishna."

239Bowing, they set out for Vrindavana,
and the devotees joyfully raised the cry of Hari.

240When Lokanatha Gosani went to Vrindavana,
the Prabhu wept in distress.

241Gadadhara weeps for his Bhugarbha;
why he sent him and why he weeps — who can understand?

242The master and the servant know, but no one else knows
in what manner the two departed.

243So [the Prabhu] joyfully disports himself in Navadvipa
together with Nityananda, Advaita and the other devotees.

244Now hear attentively what I shall write,
for the words of the Prabhu's heart are of great import.

245The two go along the road rejoicing;
in their feeling for Gaura, their hair standing on end, they fall to the ground.

246Now they walk along rapt in talk of Krishna,
now they sing aloud of Gauranga's lila.

247In humility, weeping, they say: "Prabhu, ocean of mercy,
show me even a drop of mercy, Prabhu!"

248Step by step they arrived at Rajmahal,
and the two considered how to go on.

249At that time, for fear of robbers, people did not travel;
[fearing that] the Prabhu's command would go unfulfilled, they lamented much.

250The two deliberate long: which road should we take,
by which road shall we reach the sight of Vrindavana?

251They ask people: "Brothers, which road should we take?"
And they reply: "You will not be able to get to Vrindavana."

252The two consider: "Tell me, brother:
if we go by the Tajpur road, we shall fare well."

253At dawn they set out, remembering their Prabhu,
and so they came to the village of Purnia.

254Hope rose in their hearts, and they go by that road;
after some days they arrived at Ayodhya.

255"Will such a day come that we reach Vrindavana
and see with our own eyes all its places and groves?

256The Prabhu's command will be kept and our desire fulfilled" —
thinking of all this, they weep.

257The two love each other as friends, each the other's companion —
that is why Gaura, the ocean of mercy, gave them this command.

258Then in some days they went to Lucknow,
and on the third day they arrived at Agra.25

259The Yamuna flows there; they bathed and drank,
and, counting themselves blessed, went on their way.

260At the end of the second day they reached Gokula;
seeing Krishna's birthplace, they were overwhelmed.

261"O friend, what great fortune — we have seen the birthplace!
There is no friend as merciful as Gauranga."

262Gauranga had instructed them about all the places;
the next day they entered Vrindavana.

263I make my plea at the feet of the Vaishnava Gosanis:
hear a most wondrous account.

264I wish to make known what else I have heard;
let it pain someone's heart — for me it is joy.

265Gadadhara, dear to Gauranga, is his own shakti;
let no one admit disbelief in this.

266I do not know — Gauranga himself knows;
what loss or gain there is in it, he knows.

267Gadadhara descended in the form of Krishna's beloved;
only he knows it to whom his mercy is great.

268Bhugarbha Mahashaya, whose name is Nandimukhi,
has great love for Lokanatha.

269Manjulali and Nandimukhi love each other dearly;
Gauranga let them be together — know this for certain.

270Chaitanya-chandra himself is the guru of the world,
merciful to living beings, a wish-fulfilling tree.

271He is qualified for every rasa, he is the goal and what is attained;
that is why he is worshipped by all.

272He took on the mood of a devotee and established dharma;
the Prabhu, the treasure of my life, knows his own devotees.

273As many virtues as Gaura-raya has, so many has [his] devotee;
why then does he give instruction to such a devotee?

274Speaking in dreams, he reveals everything to the devotees;
they can hold the Prabhu's virtues but cannot hold his power.

275When Lokanatha Gosani wandered through Vrindavana,
the Prabhu's power was infused into him in the course of it.26

276Like a madman he roams about, looking at everything,
and seeing the places of the lila, at times rolls on the ground.

277Seeing the beauty of Govardhana, he goes to the bank of the kundas;
seeing fields on the two kundas,27 he weeps aloud.

278He saw with his own eyes barley and wheat sown there,
and recognized in his heart which lila had been at which place.

279All the groves of the girl companions' kundas had become [fields];
now his body trembles, now he laughs.

280The next day he went to Javata, Radhika's abode,
and, recognizing one thing after another, weeps over all the pastimes.

281He recognized where each of the girl companions had lived,
and there he knew in his heart his own house.

282All the sorrow that arose within him —
he stands as if transfixed and says nothing to anyone.

283Then he went to Nanda's abode and saw all the places;
what tale of virtues there is, he alone knows.

284Then he went to Sanketa and wandered through the groves,
now bowing, now crying "Alas, alas!"

285Taking Bhugarbha by the hand, he says:
"Tell me, in which place was which lila?"

286As they spoke, both lost consciousness in ecstasy
and, crying "Radha, Radha!", weep and fall to the ground.

287That day they stayed in that place;
seeing them, the people of Vraja rejoiced.

288Having considered, all took them for great siddhas
and brought them wonderful things to eat.

289The next day, on the hill of Varshana,
the two view the places, their bodies filled with prema.

290In the morning they go to bathe in the lake,
and, deep in thought, come to the bank of the kunda.

291Having walked round again, they stay in that village;
the people of Vraja showed the two great love.

292The next day in Vrindavana they go to the Kaliya-hrada;
he says to Bhugarbha: "Do you remember, brother?"

293Recognizing the places, they go along the road,
wander through the settlement and come to Rasa-sthali.

294Seeing it, they knew that Nidhuvana lay ahead,
and, heaving deep sighs, they weep and fall to the ground.

295Going on, they reached the Chir-ghat
and saw the forest at that ghat, gazing at it.

296"Where shall we settle?" — they can find no place;
looking everywhere, they wander through all the forests.

297They saw that place, those trees and creepers,
and, settling there, they remained there.

298"Gauranga, I shall not see your feet again;
I have stayed here holding only to your command.

299The lila that the Prabhu will perform with his devotees —
of that he has deprived me and sent me here.

300When shall I see Rupa and Sanatana with my own eyes?
Then I shall count my life blessed."

301With cries of anguish he pleads at the Prabhu's feet:
"When will the Prabhu send Rupa and Sanatana?

302Then my life will hold — there is no other way;
who knows my sorrow? To whom shall I tell it?

303I have stayed, making your command my support;
fulfil my desire quickly."

304Not far from each other the two perform sadhana;
day and night they perform the sadhana that is in their hearts.

305All the people of Vraja, brahmanas and good folk,
seeing them, ponder in their minds:

306"Hear of one more wonder:
two brahmacharis have come here.

307Going to Dhira-samira we saw them,
and we understood in our hearts that they are not human.

308Sacred thread on the shoulder — how handsome they are!
What brahmachari forms, like Madana himself!

309All these days we never knew or saw the like;
are they gods or gandharvas who have descended?"

310All the people of Vraja who go hoping to see them
meet with respect and kind words from them.

311To all they say: "Follow the teaching about Krishna,"
and hearing it, all are filled with joy.

312What a manner of bhajana is theirs, all see;
whoever sees them carries out their bidding.

313People bring so many provisions from distant villages
that a hundred thousand could not eat them.

314Utterly detached, they say nothing to anyone;
all the people of Vraja hold them dear as life.

315Without seeing them for a moment, people cannot live;
whatever they command, people carry out.

316Of all the days the two lived in Vrindavana —
how much can I write, setting it forth?

317I write this account at the command of Sri Jahnava and Virachandra;
hearing all this, you will feel no pain.

318When Srimati Thakurani28 went to Vrindavana,
I, a wretch, was with her and saw it.

319Brother Ramachandra Dasa and many Vaishnavas
who were with the Thakurani saw it all.

320[They saw too] how Ishvari herself, at Rupa Gosani's place,
met all the Gosanis as they came.

321He whose hope is the feet of Sri Jahnava and Virachandra,
Nityananda Dasa, tells the Prema-vilasa.

Thus ends the seventh vilasa of the Prema-vilasa.
